newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Visco rules out another Eurotax - paper.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Visco rules out another Eurotax - paper.

text.p: The Italian government has no intention of carrying over into next year a "Euro tax" levied on Italians as part of a campaign to join the launch of a European currency union, Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco was quoted as saying on Thursday.
"It will only be paid this year. The commitment has already been made clearly and there are no reasons for going back on it," Visco told Milan daily Corriere della Sera in an interview.
The government introduced a 5.5 trillion lire Eurotax in the 1997 budget which included a one-off income tax supplement.

Asked if a change in VAT tax bands could be introduced next year to make up for the shortfall after the Eurotax is phased out, Visco said: "We shall see, we have not made plans yet. Certainly, the harmonisation of VAT is one of the issues that we have in front of us."
Visco said the tax burden would be unchanged.
"Our path will not change. We will keep the tax burden unchanged, stable. Obviously net of the extraordinary contribution for Europe which is a once-off." Milan newsroom +392-66102321
